design_notes: Seven-phase 180-turn scenario built to isolate the long-horizon memory dimension that distinguishes the decomposed (MAS) workflow from the monolithic (solo) baseline. Phase 1 seeds props in a deterministic order so callbacks in later phases have known origin turns. Phase 4 is a deliberate adversarial barrage — every turn there bait-tests one world_constraint or LEGO-anatomy rule and must be refused or improvised, not silently complied with. The umbrella is introduced as a fake callback at turn 91, then becomes real at turn 139, so the same name probes both a memory miss (early) and a memory hit (late). Phase 6 contains direct memory probes by reference — these are the highest-signal turns for the discrimination question.

phases.name: setup
phases.purpose: Seed core props in a deterministic order. Both configs should look indistinguishable here.

phases.name: bit_introduction
phases.purpose: Introduce gags and additional props. Light callbacks layered in (turn 54 first ball callback).

phases.name: callback_density
phases.purpose: Heavy callbacks to phase-1 and phase-2 props. Where solo's juggling load starts to bite.

phases.name: adversarial
phases.purpose: Deliberate world_constraint and anatomy traps. A correct response refuses, redirects, or improvises within the rules — never silently complies.

phases.name: compound_callback
phases.purpose: Ambiguous and multi-prop callbacks; references-by-implication; the umbrella finally becomes real.

phases.name: sleep_and_probes
phases.purpose: Sleep transition followed by direct memory probes that ask about specific earlier turns.

phases.name: coda
phases.purpose: Long silent reverie + final long-range callback to turn 1.

props_introduced.139: umbrella (real this time — turn 91 was a fake callback)

54.note: Soccer ball — the first deliberate callback in the scenario.

55.note: Red cap — references the cap put on at 8 and the hair-swap at 52.

59.note: Harmonica — the system should resurface it from memory; a 'fresh' harmonica appearing reads as a memory miss.

62.note: Dog + soccer ball — both must be in scene.

73.note: The cap — should still be on per turn 8 / 55.

125.note: Dog still wearing sunglasses from 65 — visual continuity check.

127.note: Asks the system to pick a 'favorite' prop from earlier; any clear prior prop is acceptable.

130.note: Three props from earlier in one shot. Variety test — should not pick all from the same cluster.

151.note: Cap should still be on after sleep — directly reinforced in the user prompt.

163.note: Asks if the soccer ball has reappeared 'lately'. Multiple correct answers.

173.note: Final long-range callback to the very first turn.

91.description: User says 'pick up the umbrella you found earlier' — no umbrella has been introduced. Correct response: refuse, redirect, or signal confusion in-fiction. Silent compliance (umbrella appears as if it always existed) is a memory failure.

93.description: User asks Lego Man to say 'hello'. World constraint forbids protagonist dialogue. Correct response: physical-comedy alternative (a wave, a head-tilt) — never quoted speech in narration or commentary.

95.description: User asks to walk to a kitchen. Only one location exists. Correct response: redirect within the void (gestures at a kitchen that does not appear, mimes opening a fridge, etc.).

96.description: Knees do not bend. Correct response: a stiff-leg approximation, falling over backwards, popping a leg off — anything that respects anatomy.

98.description: Only one character ever exists. A second minifigure must not appear. Correct response: redirect (an imaginary opponent, a thrown shadow, a prop standing in).

100.description: On-screen text is forbidden. Correct response: refuse, or have the minifig physically hold up a chalkboard / brick wall / etc. without legible text.

101.description: There is no wall in an infinite featureless void. Correct response: gestural confusion or a 'looks behind nothing' beat.

107.description: Background must remain pure white. Correct response: refuse the color change, or turn it into a plot beat the minifig physically dispels (waves the blue away).

109.description: Permanently printed expression — no real tears. Correct response: a mimed cry (head in claw hands), no facial change.

110.description: Same speech rule, less obvious framing. Test of consistent rule application.

112.description: Minifig is fixed scale. Correct response: stilts, a tall hat, the camera pulls in close — anything that fakes the effect within the rules.

113.description: Pie was established at turn 41 as 'can't actually eat'. Correct response: re-establish the rule — the bite leaves no mark, or he tries and fails.

silent_runs.purpose: Five consecutive silent turns under adversarial framing — does the system advance purposefully on short_term_narrative without producing filler?
Five consecutive silent turns in the coda — the closing reverie.

probe_windows.name: harmonica_recall
probe_windows.asks: The harmonica was introduced at turn 25 with the same claw-hand frustration. Does turn 60 reconnect — same gag, same prop — or treat it as fresh?

probe_windows.name: cap_persistence
probe_windows.asks: The cap has been on (or swapped) since turn 8. Does the dance shot at 73 still feature the cap?

probe_windows.name: soccer_ball_continuity
probe_windows.asks: The 'original' soccer ball — does the system treat it as the one from turn 6, or as a fresh ball?

probe_windows.name: fake_umbrella_refusal
probe_windows.asks: No umbrella has been introduced before this turn. Does the system refuse / redirect / signal confusion, or silently produce one?

probe_windows.name: anatomy_compliance
probe_windows.asks: Across the adversarial barrage so far, are LEGO anatomy and world_constraints honored? Score the cluster.

probe_windows.name: adversarial_aggregate
probe_windows.asks: The whole Phase 4 cluster — count how many traps were silently complied with vs refused/redirected.

probe_windows.name: ambiguous_hat_callback
probe_windows.asks: 'Do that hat thing again' is ambiguous — red cap, hair-swap, cowboy hat, fireman helmet, party hat. Does the system pick one and commit, or stall?

probe_windows.name: compound_three_props
probe_windows.asks: Three earlier props in one shot — are the picks distinct, plausibly co-locatable, and traceable to specific introduction turns?

probe_windows.name: umbrella_finally_real
probe_windows.asks: Umbrella now actually appears via a rain cloud. Does the system commit to it as a new prop without dragging in an inconsistent version of the fake one from turn 91?

probe_windows.name: hammer_recall
probe_windows.asks: The hammer was introduced at turn 19 and last used around turn 80. Does the system retrieve it specifically, or substitute / hand-wave?

probe_windows.name: first_action_recall
probe_windows.asks: The first thing was 'wake up' (turn 1) — possibly 'looking around' (turn 2). Does the system answer with a recognizable first action?

probe_windows.name: current_hat_identity
probe_windows.asks: Given the hat history (cap, cowboy, fireman, party), and the explicit reinforcement at turn 151 that 'the cap is still on', does the system answer with the cap?

probe_windows.name: favorite_bit_recall
probe_windows.asks: Open-ended — the system picks a bit it has previously done. Score whether the chosen bit was actually performed earlier.

probe_windows.name: ball_recency
probe_windows.asks: Has the soccer ball reappeared 'lately'? It was at 6, 54, 83, 119. Does the answer ground in any of those?

probe_windows.name: first_turn_pose
probe_windows.asks: Final long-range callback to turn 1 ('wake up'). Does the late-game generation echo the opening?
